question: Find the equation of a straight line which is perpendicular to the line x − 3y + 2 = 0 and passes through the mid-point of the line joining the points (3, −2) and (−1,5) .
modelAnswer:
Gradient of x − 3y + 2 = 0: 3y = x + 2 → y = x/3 + 2/3, so m₁ = 1/3.
Perpendicular gradient: m₂ = −1/m₁ = −3.

Mid-point of (3, −2) and (−1, 5): ((3 − 1)/2, (−2 + 5)/2) = (1, 3/2).

Equation: y − 3/2 = −3(x − 1)
2y − 3 = −6x + 6
6x + 2y − 9 = 0 (or y = −3x + 9/2).

question: Show that f(x) = 5e⁻⁵ˣ, 0 ≤ x ≤ ∞ is a probability density function, hence find the probability for x ≤ 3.
modelAnswer:
A function is a p.d.f. if f(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the range and the total area under it is 1.
1. 5e⁻⁵ˣ > 0 for every x, since an exponential is always positive.
2. ∫₀^∞ 5e⁻⁵ˣ dx = [−e⁻⁵ˣ]₀^∞ = (0) − (−1) = 1.
Both conditions hold, so f(x) is a probability density function.

P(X ≤ 3) = ∫₀³ 5e⁻⁵ˣ dx = [−e⁻⁵ˣ]₀³ = −e⁻¹⁵ + 1 = 1 − e⁻¹⁵.
e⁻¹⁵ ≈ 3.06 × 10⁻⁷, so P(X ≤ 3) ≈ 0.9999997 (practically 1).

question: Find the focus of the parabola y² = 3(x + 1).
modelAnswer:
Compare with the standard form Y² = 4aX, where Y = y and X = x + 1.
4a = 3 → a = 3/4.
The vertex is where X = 0 and Y = 0: (−1, 0).
For Y² = 4aX the focus is at X = a, Y = 0, so x + 1 = 3/4 → x = −1/4.
Focus: (−1/4, 0).
(The directrix is X = −a: x + 1 = −3/4, so x = −7/4.)

question:
(a) Obtain the equation of the conic whose parametric equations are y = 5 + 4 tan θ,
x = 7 + 3 sec θ and describe it completely.
modelAnswer:
sec θ = (x − 7)/3 and tan θ = (y − 5)/4.
Using sec²θ − tan²θ = 1:
(x − 7)²/9 − (y − 5)²/16 = 1.

This is a hyperbola. Comparing with (x − h)²/a² − (y − k)²/b² = 1:
• Centre: (7, 5); a = 3, b = 4.
• Transverse axis: along the line y = 5 (parallel to the x-axis), length 2a = 6.
• Conjugate axis: along x = 7, length 2b = 8.
• Vertices: (7 ± 3, 5) = (10, 5) and (4, 5).
• c² = a² + b² = 9 + 16 = 25 → c = 5. Foci: (7 ± 5, 5) = (12, 5) and (2, 5).
• Eccentricity: e = c/a = 5/3.
• Directrices: x = 7 ± a/e = 7 ± 9/5, that is x = 8.8 and x = 5.2.
• Asymptotes: y − 5 = ±(4/3)(x − 7), that is 4x − 3y − 13 = 0 and 4x + 3y − 43 = 0.
• Length of each latus rectum: 2b²/a = 32/3.

question:
(b) Write the following in polar form
(i) 3x+2y= 8, (ii) x² = √(x² + y²)
modelAnswer:
Use x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ and x² + y² = r².

(i) 3r cos θ + 2r sin θ = 8
r(3 cos θ + 2 sin θ) = 8, or r = 8/(3 cos θ + 2 sin θ).

(ii) r² cos²θ = √(r²) = r (taking r ≥ 0).
Divide by r (r ≠ 0): r cos²θ = 1, so r = sec²θ.
(The origin, r = 0, also satisfies the original equation.)

subject: Mathematics
question:
(a) Obtain the equation of the conic whose parametric equations are y = k + 2t,
x = h + t² and obtain condition for which the line y = mx + c touches it.
modelAnswer:
From y = k + 2t: t = (y − k)/2.
Substitute into x = h + t²: x − h = (y − k)²/4.
(y − k)² = 4(x − h).
This is a parabola with vertex (h, k), axis y = k, and a = 1 (focus at (h + 1, k)).

Condition for tangency:
From the line, x = (y − c)/m (m ≠ 0). Substitute:
(y − k)² = 4[(y − c)/m − h]
m(y − k)² = 4(y − c) − 4mh
my² − 2mky + mk² − 4y + 4c + 4mh = 0
my² − (2mk + 4)y + (mk² + 4c + 4mh) = 0.

The line touches the parabola when this quadratic in y has equal roots (discriminant = 0):
(2mk + 4)² − 4m(mk² + 4c + 4mh) = 0
4m²k² + 16mk + 16 − 4m²k² − 16mc − 16m²h = 0
Divide by 16: mk + 1 − mc − m²h = 0.

Condition: mc = 1 + mk − m²h, that is c = k − mh + 1/m.
(Check: with h = k = 0 this becomes c = 1/m, the known condition for y = mx + c to touch y² = 4x.)

question: (b) Describe the locus of the points P(x, y) equidistant from the points A(3, −2) and B(−3, 5).
modelAnswer:
PA = PB, so PA² = PB²:
(x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = (x + 3)² + (y − 5)²
x² − 6x + 9 + y² + 4y + 4 = x² + 6x + 9 + y² − 10y + 25
−6x + 4y + 13 = 6x − 10y + 34
−12x + 14y − 21 = 0
12x − 14y + 21 = 0.

Description: the locus is a straight line, the perpendicular bisector of AB.
• It passes through the mid-point of AB, (0, 3/2): 12(0) − 14(3/2) + 21 = 0 ✓.
• Its gradient is 12/14 = 6/7; the gradient of AB is (5 + 2)/(−3 − 3) = −7/6, and (6/7)(−7/6) = −1, so it is perpendicular to AB.

subject: Mathematics
question: (a) Find the equation of the tangent to the ellipse (x − h)²/a² + (y − k)²/b² = 1, at the point (x₁, y₁). Hence, obtain the equation of the tangent to the ellipse (x + 2)²/16 + y²/4 = 1, at the point (−2, 2).
modelAnswer:
Differentiate implicitly:
2(x − h)/a² + 2(y − k)/b² × dy/dx = 0
dy/dx = −b²(x − h)/[a²(y − k)].
At (x₁, y₁) the gradient is −b²(x₁ − h)/[a²(y₁ − k)].

Tangent: y − y₁ = −b²(x₁ − h)/[a²(y₁ − k)] × (x − x₁).
Multiply out: (y − y₁)(y₁ − k)/b² + (x − x₁)(x₁ − h)/a² = 0.
Write x − x₁ = (x − h) − (x₁ − h) and y − y₁ = (y − k) − (y₁ − k):
(x − h)(x₁ − h)/a² + (y − k)(y₁ − k)/b² = (x₁ − h)²/a² + (y₁ − k)²/b² = 1 (because (x₁, y₁) lies on the ellipse).

Tangent at (x₁, y₁): (x − h)(x₁ − h)/a² + (y − k)(y₁ − k)/b² = 1.

Application: (x + 2)²/16 + y²/4 = 1 has h = −2, k = 0, a² = 16, b² = 4.
Check the point (−2, 2): 0/16 + 4/4 = 1 ✓, so it is on the ellipse.
Tangent: (x + 2)(−2 + 2)/16 + (y)(2)/4 = 1
0 + y/2 = 1 → y = 2.
(This makes sense: (−2, 2) is the top end of the minor axis, where the tangent is horizontal.)

question: (b) Sketch the curve r = 2(1 + sin 3θ) in polar form for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 360⁰.
modelAnswer:
Table of values (r = 2 + 2 sin 3θ):
θ: 0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°, 90°, 105°, 120°, 135°, 150°, 165°, 180°
r: 2, 3.41, 4, 3.41, 2, 0.59, 0, 0.59, 2, 3.41, 4, 3.41, 2
The pattern then repeats every 120°: r = 4 at θ = 30°, 150°, 270°; r = 0 at θ = 90°, 210°, 330°; r = 2 at θ = 0°, 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°.

Key features of the sketch:
• r is never negative (0 ≤ r ≤ 4), so the curve lies wholly in the region r ≤ 4.
• It has three large loops (petals) pointing along θ = 30°, 150° and 270°, each reaching r = 4.
• The curve passes through the pole at θ = 90°, 210° and 330°, where it forms cusps pointing inward.
• It crosses the initial line (θ = 0°) and θ = 180° at r = 2.
• Since sin 3θ has period 120°, the curve has three-fold symmetry, and it is symmetric about the line θ = 90° (the y-axis).
Join the plotted points smoothly to obtain a three-lobed curve (a 'three-leaved' limaçon-type shape).

subject: Mathematics
question:
(a) Two numbers are selected at random from integers 10 to 40, both inclusive, repetition being allowed. Find the probability that:
(i) Both are multiples of 5 (ii) both are powers of 2
(iii) One is power of 2 and the other is a multiple of 5. What are the corresponding probabilities if repetition is not allowed?
modelAnswer:
Integers from 10 to 40 inclusive: 40 − 10 + 1 = 31.
Multiples of 5: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 → 7 numbers.
Powers of 2: 16, 32 → 2 numbers. (No number is both.)
The two numbers are taken in order (first and second selection).

With repetition allowed (31 × 31 = 961 equally likely outcomes):
(i) P(both multiples of 5) = (7/31)(7/31) = 49/961 ≈ 0.0510.
(ii) P(both powers of 2) = (2/31)(2/31) = 4/961 ≈ 0.0042.
(iii) P(one power of 2, other multiple of 5) = (2/31)(7/31) + (7/31)(2/31) = 28/961 ≈ 0.0291.

Without repetition (31 × 30 = 930 outcomes):
(i) (7/31)(6/30) = 42/930 = 7/155 ≈ 0.0452.
(ii) (2/31)(1/30) = 2/930 = 1/465 ≈ 0.0022.
(iii) (2/31)(7/30) + (7/31)(2/30) = 28/930 = 14/465 ≈ 0.0301.
(Counting unordered pairs gives the same results without repetition, e.g. (i) ⁷C₂/³¹C₂ = 21/465 = 7/155.)

subject: Mathematics
question:
(b) If a card is randomly selected from a deck of cards, find the probability that it is
(i) A spade or a diamond; (ii) An ace or a heart.
modelAnswer:
A standard deck has 52 cards: 4 suits of 13, with 4 aces.

(i) Spades and diamonds cannot happen together (mutually exclusive):
P(spade or diamond) = 13/52 + 13/52 = 26/52 = 1/2.

(ii) Aces and hearts overlap (the ace of hearts), so use P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B):
P(ace or heart) = 4/52 + 13/52 − 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.

subject: Mathematics
question:
(a) Three balls are drawn at random without replacement from a bag containing 10 black, 13 white and 11 red balls. Find the probability that
(i) the balls are of the same color (ii) 2 of the balls are black and one is white.
modelAnswer:
Total balls = 10 + 13 + 11 = 34.
Number of ways to choose 3: ³⁴C₃ = (34 × 33 × 32)/6 = 5984.

(i) Same colour:
All black: ¹⁰C₃ = 120; all white: ¹³C₃ = 286; all red: ¹¹C₃ = 165.
Total = 120 + 286 + 165 = 571.
P(same colour) = 571/5984 ≈ 0.0954.

(ii) 2 black and 1 white: ¹⁰C₂ × ¹³C₁ = 45 × 13 = 585.
P = 585/5984 ≈ 0.0978.
